Estimate biological means at age from length-stratified sampling

Source: R/age_means.R
age_means.Rd

Estimate biological means at age from length-stratified sampling

age_means(
  length_totals,
  aged,
  metrics,
  strata = character(),
  by = strata,
  ages = NULL
)

Arguments

length_totals

Data frame with expanded fish counts total for each length group and stratum. Rows sharing a stratum and length are summed.

aged

Data frame with one row per biological sample. Include age, the same length group labels, stratum keys, and the requested traits. Records with missing age are excluded from the age-length key.

metrics

Names of numeric or logical trait columns. Use binary mature for proportion mature, or weight in kilograms for mean weight. Requesting "length" gives mean length using the bin labels.

strata

Columns defining the groups within which to expand length samples. Supply all grouping keys needed to match the design, including time and spatial identifiers where applicable.

by

Grouping columns to retain, as a subset of strata. The default retains all strata. An empty vector pools all strata.

ages

Optional nonnegative whole ages to report. The default uses all observed age labels. Supply ages to report support when no fish were aged.

Value

A keyed data table with the requested by columns, age, metric, estimate, n (records with observed traits and positive expansion), and status. Statuses include "ok", "missing_length_total", "no_aging_support", "missing_trait", and "no_weighted_fish". Unsupported means are missing.

Details

Each aged fish represents its stratum-length total divided by the number of usable ages in that cell. Sum weighted trait values and weights at age across strata before dividing. This is the point estimator of Morgan and Hoenig (1997) for maturity and Morgan (1999) for weight. It assumes representative aging within each stratum and length.

Age counts use all available ages, independently of trait availability. An unknown length total or positive length total without an age sample makes the pooled composition unsupported. Missing traits among weighted aged fish make the corresponding age and trait estimate unavailable.

References

Morgan, M. J. and Hoenig, J. M. (1997). Estimating maturity-at-age from length stratified sampling. Journal of Northwest Atlantic Fishery Science, 21, 51–63. https://doi.org/10.2960/J.v21.a4

Morgan, M. J. (1999). The effect of a change in perception of length distribution of a population on maturity-at-age, weight-at-age and spawning stock biomass. Journal of Northwest Atlantic Fishery Science, 25, 141–150. https://doi.org/10.2960/J.v25.a13

Examples

length_totals <- data.frame(length = c(20, 40), total = c(90, 10))
aged <- data.frame(age = 3, length = c(20, 40), mature = c(0, 1),
                   weight = c(1, 3))
age_means(length_totals, aged, c("weight", "mature"))
